entry.v: core library version that produced the entry

coreToPage.description: A core instance announces itself on window.__COMVI__ at construction time when the devtools capability is present in its module graph and exposeGlobal is on (default true in browsers). In 0.4 the root entry always carried that capability. From 0.5 the single entry is the base host, so the capability arrives through the devtools() installer, attachDevtools, or a plugin installer that ensures devtools (in-context-editor); an app that composes none of them is invisible to the extension by construction, not by failure.
probeOrder: Array.isArray(g) -> g.push({v, i}) — raw v2 queue array, or a consumer's array-masquerading hook whose OWN push/remove shadow Array.prototype

typeof g.push === 'function' && typeof g.remove === 'function' -> g.push({v, i}) — v2 hook object, including dual-protocol hooks that also expose register; probed BEFORE legacy so new/new never downgrades to v1
typeof g.register === 'function' -> g.register(instanceId, instance) — register WITHOUT remove means a genuine v1 legacy registry; two-arg call so its get(id) resolves
!g -> window.__COMVI__ = [{v, i}] — install a fresh queue array
truthy non-conforming global -> left untouched, exposure skipped (never clobber)
coreToPage.removal: destroy() removes identity-based and probes in the SAME order as exposure: Array.isArray(g) -> a masquerading hook's OWN remove (own property, callable) gets g.remove(entry), otherwise indexOf/splice of the SAME entry object; then a non-array hook -> g.remove(entry); then legacy registry -> g.unregister(instanceId). Array.isArray FIRST is load-bearing: a page that extends Array.prototype with a remove(index) polyfill would otherwise be handed the entry OBJECT, which coerces to index 0 and splices someone else's live entry with nothing thrown. All discovery and removal is wrapped in try/catch — it must never break construction or destroy.
coreToPage.instanceIds: The default id is `comvi-<n>`, counted once per PAGE: the sequence lives in a `Symbol.for("comvi.core.instanceCounter")` slot on globalThis, so two copies of core on one page (CDN global plus bundled npm copy, or a binding pinned to another patch) continue one sequence instead of both minting `comvi-1`. Minting never reads `window.__COMVI__`: an id is chosen before the protocol is probed, so a hostile hook can neither throw out of construction nor make minting spin. An explicitly passed instanceId is used as given and may still collide, which the consumer dedupes on drain (see pageToExtension.idCollisions). `instanceId` is public: it appears on the instance and in the extension's ActivateResult.

pageToExtension.description: The consumer (in-context editor / Chrome extension) MUST drain-and-swap on boot: if window.__COMVI__ is an array, SWAP the global to its hook object FIRST, then drain the snapshot ({v, i} envelopes AND bare legacy instances). The swapped-in hook implements BOTH protocols: v2 (push/remove) and v1 legacy (register/unregister/get/instances view), so an old core landing later still attaches via register.
pageToExtension.hookShape: Object.assign([], { __comviEditorHook: true, push, remove, register, unregister, get, instances, version }) — array-masquerading so new core's Array.isArray-first probe routes through the hook's OWN push. Do not drop the array masquerade or reorder core's probe independently: they are a matched pair.
pageToExtension.markerRule: The hook carries `__comviEditorHook === true` so that whichever consumer installs first (in-context editor or extension detector) is REUSED by the other instead of swapping again. It is not proof of a hook: it is page-writable, and a page that pollutes Object.prototype.__comviEditorHook marks every object. A consumer MUST therefore validate requiredMembers before adopting a marked global, MUST probe Array.isArray BEFORE the marker (so a polluted prototype cannot make a raw queue array look like an installed hook), and MUST read the marker and the entry's `i` as OWN properties rather than with `in`. A marked global that fails requiredMembers is treated as whatever it otherwise looks like — a v1 legacy registry if it duck-types as one, else a truthy non-conforming global: left untouched, never adopted, never read, and never a thrown error.
pageToExtension.idCollisions: Consumer hooks key instances on `instance.instanceId`, so two cores that announced the same id must not overwrite one another. track() DEDUPES a colliding id, tracking the later instance under `<id>#<n>` (suffix appended to the ORIGINAL id, never to an already-suffixed one) and warning on the console, so both instances stay discoverable and countable. The deduped instance is addressable by the id it announced only while that is unambiguous: get(id) falls back to the single `<id>#<n>` entry when nothing holds the exact key, and returns undefined when two or more do, in which case the caller must name the deduped key. remove()/untrack() delete the map slot ONLY while it still holds THAT instance, and unregister(id) resolves the instance that CLAIMED the id through register(id, instance) before falling back to whoever holds the key, so neither can evict a different live instance.
pageToExtension.legacyRegistryBoot: If the pre-existing global is the v1 registry object (register fn / instances Map), read its instances map into the hook, then swap; keep a COMVI_READY listener on the drained legacy object as the v1 shim.

versionPairing.old-core+new-extension: supported — the extension's legacy shim reads .instances and COMVI_READY, and its dual-protocol hook accepts register()
versionPairing.new-core+old-extension: UNSUPPORTED — the one broken pairing; the old extension never drains the queue array. Release notes pin the minimum extension version.
versionPairing.old-core+new-core-same-page: supported — new core detects the legacy object (register without remove) and calls register(id, instance); the new extension's hook speaks both protocols. Ids may collide (old core also minted `comvi-<n>`); the hook's dedupe and identity-safe removal keep both instances discoverable (see pageToExtension.idCollisions).
versionPairing.new-core+new-core-same-page: supported — two copies of new core (CDN global plus bundled npm copy, or a binding on another patch) both push onto one queue/hook. The second copy skips an id a consumer hook already tracks, and a consumer draining a raw queue dedupes colliding ids, so both instances stay discoverable and destroying one leaves the other tracked.
versionPairing.new-extension-0.5.1+core-0.5.0: detected, not activatable — the extension no longer carries an editor; the popup explains

editorLoader.installedBy: the devtools capability (`.use(devtools())` / `attachDevtools`) at exposure time in a browser, once per page; never by a base instance; the composite (`core/full.ts`) installs it too
editorLoader.replacement: a later core installs over an existing slot only when its `protocol` is strictly greater; same or lower protocol reuses the existing slot. The load promise lives under the second key `Symbol.for("comvi.devtools.editorLoad")`, so a replacement reuses a pending or finished load and never creates a second <script>; a core that reuses a slot with a different editorVersion warns once in development
editorLoader.hookCompatibility: TWO-DIRECTIONAL. (a) Hook fields released under a protocol are never removed or retyped — new fields only; a protocol bump adds fields or load() result members, never changes protocol-1 semantics. (b) The editor treats ANY protocol ≥ 1 as usable, reads only the protocol-1 fields it knows, and ignores unknown fields; it never refuses a newer hook. (c) The hook reads nothing off window.ComviInContextEditor except `activate` (to decide already-loaded / no-global) and, optionally, `version`. Older editor + newer hook is a permanent pairing (editorVersion pins and the browser cache guarantee it), as is newer editor + older hook

shape.protocol: 1 — integer; the hook↔editor protocol version. Every future editor must work with every released protocol, and every released editor with every future protocol (see hookCompatibility)
shape.sdkVersion: the @comvi/core version that installed the slot (string, __VERSION__)
shape.editorVersion: the pin from devtools({ editorVersion }) when it is a string primitive matching ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$, otherwise "latest" — the exact string used in the URL. The option is read once; a non-string (an object with toString/valueOf, a String object, a number) is never coerced and falls back to "latest"; an option whose getter throws installs no slot and construction carries on
shape.url: the full URL the hook will load; host and path are constants in core: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@comvi/plugin-in-context-editor@<editorVersion>/dist/standalone.iife.js — plus, ONLY when editorVersion is "latest", the cache salt `?comvi=<floor(Date.now()/3600000)>` (hour bucket; bounds browser staleness to ≤ 1 h). An exact pin has no query string (immutable file). The salt is computed at load() time, so `url` on the slot is the salt-free base and the result's `url` is what was requested
shape.load(): returns Promise<EditorLoadResult>; idempotent — the first call creates ONE <script crossorigin="anonymous"> and caches the promise under the second key; later calls return the same promise, while the load is pending and after it succeeded; a settled failure is NOT cached, so a retry after the user fixed the CSP creates a fresh script. Internal timeout 10 000 ms: strictly inside the popup's 15 s activation budget and the worker's 30 s pending-session TTL, so the hook's failure code — not the popup's generic "did not respond" — is what the user sees

EditorLoadResult.ok: true | false. Every result carries the keys ok, url, sdkVersion, protocol, editorVersion, code and host; a key that does not apply holds undefined — it is not omitted
EditorLoadResult.url: the URL requested (with the cache salt on "latest"); the salt-free slot url when the editor was already on the page and nothing was requested
EditorLoadResult.editorVersion: the editor's own reported version when ok (window.ComviInContextEditor.version, present from editor 0.5.1); undefined for an older editor and when ok is false
EditorLoadResult.code: when ok is false: "csp-blocked" | "load-error" | "timeout" | "no-global"; undefined when ok is true
EditorLoadResult.host: when ok is false: "cdn.jsdelivr.net" — the host the popup tells the user to allow; undefined when ok is true
EditorLoadResult.message: optional, human-readable, ≤ 256 chars; reserved — core 0.5.1 never sets it

failureCodes.csp-blocked: the page's own policy refused the script. Two cases: (1) a `securitypolicyviolation` event on document whose disposition is not "report" (an engine that omits the field is taken to enforce), effectiveDirective script-src-elem or script-src, and a blockedURI that starts with the editor URL (Chromium reports the full URL, query included) or equals the CDN origin, observed before the script's error event — it takes precedence over load-error; a report-only violation or one under another directive does not count; (2) the page enforces Trusted Types (`require-trusted-types-for 'script'`) and assigning the script's src threw (only that assignment; a throw from the insertion is load-error). The remedy differs: (1) allow https://cdn.jsdelivr.net in script-src; (2) the site's `default` Trusted Types policy must return that script URL from createScriptURL (the loader assigns src as a plain string, so no other policy sees it) — allowing the host alone does not help
failureCodes.load-error: the <script> element fired `error` with no matching CSP violation (DNS, offline, 404 for a bad pin, corporate filter), or the script could not be inserted (no document, no root element)
failureCodes.timeout: neither load nor error within 10 000 ms (the script element is removed; a later load() starts fresh)
failureCodes.no-global: `load` fired but window.ComviInContextEditor is not an object with an activate() function (a wrong file served, or a corrupted copy)

shape.already-loaded: if no load is pending or finished and window.ComviInContextEditor already exists when load() is called (an old extension injected its bundled copy, or the site bundled the standalone itself), load() resolves a fresh { ok: true } result immediately without creating a script; its url is the salt-free slot url

editorLoader.detectorToPage: the detector reads the slot synchronously for status (`editorLoader: { protocol, sdkVersion, editorVersion } | null`; a slot is one whose `protocol` is an integer ≥ 1 and whose `load` is a function) and, when the page has no `ComviInContextEditor` with an `activate()` function, calls `load()` inside the comvi-extension:activate handler before activate(), under try/catch and its own 12 000 ms limit (above the hook's 10 000 ms, inside the popup's 15 s budget). A throwing or rejecting `load()`, an answer that is not `{ ok: true }` with a code from failureCodes, or an answer whose fields throw is a page fault, reported as { success:false, code:"load-error" }; a silent `load()` is { code:"timeout" }; `{ ok: true }` with no editor on the page is { code:"no-global" }; no slot and no editor is the extension's own { code:"no-loader" } (an SDK older than 0.5.1). The detector NEVER reads `url` and never creates a script element. A page that already carries the editor is activated without calling `load()`. A newer activate command, or a deactivate, retires an activation that is still waiting for `load()`. Only the code is forwarded, on comvi-extension:activated as { success:false, code }; the answer's code is read once, and its host, message and every other field stay in the page. An activate() that throws is reported as { success:false } without the thrown text. The popup words every reason and remedy itself, with its OWN constant host string
editorLoader.pageToEditor: the standalone editor reads the slot at boot (after ensureComviHook) and records { protocol, sdkVersion } in getStatus().hook; it must tolerate a missing slot (old extension injected it) and ANY protocol ≥ 1, including ones newer than itself, per hookCompatibility
editorLoader.extensionStatusAdditions: StatusResponsePayload gains editorLoader?: { protocol: number; sdkVersion?: string; editorVersion?: string } | null and editorVersion?: string; EditorActivatedPayload is { success, code?, instanceId?, collectContext? } and carries no free text (no error, no host). The bridge reads every property of a page-authored object exactly once, under try/catch, and sanitizes by type and length (protocol an integer ≥ 1, versions ≤ 64 characters, code ≤ 32). The service worker tells the popup a code only: one of csp-blocked | load-error | timeout | no-global | no-loader when the page reported it, otherwise its own `failed`, or `unconfirmed` when the acknowledgement did not match the pending session. The popup shows a page-reported SDK or editor version only when it matches ^\d{1,4}\.\d{1,4}\.\d{1,4}(-[a-z]{1,8}(\.\d{1,10})?)?$ and is at most 32 characters; no other page-authored string is ever rendered

versionPairing.new-extension+sdk-0.5.0: detected, slot absent → popup names the 0.5.1 requirement; Enable disabled
versionPairing.old-extension+sdk-0.5.1: supported — the old extension injects its bundled editor; the slot is unused
versionPairing.old-editor+newer-hook: supported forever — the editor reads protocol-1 fields only; the hook never removes or retypes them
versionPairing.two-cores: one slot per page; highest protocol wins; the load promise is shared under the second key, so one script
versionPairing.umd-composite: the CDN global (core/full.ts) always loads @latest; pinning exists only through devtools({ editorVersion })
